 Fantasy football Week 10 Start 'Em & Sit 'Em: Ollie Gordon smashes bounce back matchup vs. Colts
 Plus, trade deadline fallout opens the door for a Jonathan Taylor rebound against Miami, and the Rams DST headlines the top defensive plays
 By
 Jamey Eisenberg 
 Nov 12, 2026
 at
 1:52 am ET 
 •
 2 min read
 Imagn Images Imagn Images 
 The biggest story this week was what happened at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, and we had some major moves that altered things in Fantasy and reality. The biggest trades for Fantasy managers involved Kirk Cousins going to Minnesota, Keenan Allen going to the 49ers and Josh Downs going to Kansas City. 
 But we also know a trade that didn't happen was impactful: Jonathan Taylor remaining in Indianapolis. Now that we know Taylor is staying with the Colts, we need him to return to his dominant ways. 
 He performed poorly in his past two games against Jacksonville and Dallas with 9.4 PPR points or less in each outing. Struggling against the Jaguars is understandable given their strong defense, but it was frustrating to see Taylor struggle against the Cowboys. 
 Hopefully, Taylor was bothered by the trade speculation, and now he can play without any hesitation. He has a great matchup in Week 10 against Miami, and the Dolphins are No. 6 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing running backs. A running back has scored at least 12 PPR points in every game against the Dolphins this season, including four guys scoring at least 19.4 PPR points. 
 That's the level of production we expect from Taylor on a weekly basis, and he scored at least 19 PPR points in five of his first seven games. The Colts stripped down their offense with the trades of Allen and Downs, along with an earlier deal sending standout offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to Seattle, but I'm still confident in Taylor. 
 As long as he's healthy and active, Taylor has top-10 upside in all leagues. I would have preferred to see him traded to a better team, but the Colts kept Taylor and now need to keep him playing at a high level for the rest of the year.

 I was hesitant to trust Gordon when he took over for De'Von Achane (knee) in Week 3, but he performed well in his first four games as Miami's lead running back, scoring at least 14.5 PPR points in each outing, along with four touchdowns. Gordon struggled in each of his past two games against New England and Detroit, scoring 7.4 PPR points or less in each contest, but he should get back on track in Week 10 at Indianapolis. The Colts are No. 8 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing running backs, and six running backs have scored at least 12.8 PPR points against Indianapolis this season. Three of those performances came in the past two games from Bhayshul Tuten, Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Javonte Williams, which coincides with the Colts trading standout defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. The Jaguars running backs combined for 28 carries for 158 yards and two touchdowns, plus three catches for 62 yards and a touchdown on three targets. The Cowboys running backs combined for 32 carries for 178 yards and a touchdown, plus four catches for 23 yards on six targets. Gordon might get a boost in the passing game with Kyle McCord taking over for Malik Willis (groin), but Gordon is dependent on volume and finding the endzone. He has at least 17 total touches in four consecutive games, and his best games this season have come when he scored a touchdown. I'm expecting another standout game from Gordon in Week 10, and he has top-10 upside in all leagues.
